T316-Arm-C DELIVERABLE 2 — review of untracked/T316-seeded/parallel-fixpoint.md only.

=== WHAT I READ ===
untracked/T316-seeded/parallel-fixpoint.md — a seeded copy of T312's prose write-up.
docs/epistemic/CLAIMS.md — register verification for GLOBAL.F2, GLOBAL.B1-MULTIFIX.

=== DEFECTS FOUND (6) ===

1. [CLASS: cite-tag-status] "GLOBAL.F2 is PROVEN per docs/epistemic/CLAIMS.md"
   (Design § Jacobi vs Gauss-Seidel). CLAIMS.md line 338 shows GLOBAL.F2 status =
   CLAIMED, not PROVEN. The row is explicitly orphaned: "Status left CLAIMED —
   the ruling refutes the justification, it does not falsify the finisher."
   Rationale: direct contradiction with the register.

2. [CLASS: false-mathematical-claim] "Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel converge to the
   same (unique) fixpoint" (Design § Jacobi vs Gauss-Seidel). The register shows
   this is false: GLOBAL.B1-MULTIFIX (MEASUREMENT) documents that the L map has
   MULTIPLE fixpoints — "re-converge from +N lands above canonical." Gauss-Seidel
   can land at different fixpoints depending on sweep order. The fixpoint is not
   unique, and Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel are not guaranteed to converge to the same
   one when multiple exist. Rationale: GLOBAL.B1-MULTIFIX (CLAIMS.md §2.2) is
   a direct measurement contradicting the uniqueness claim.

3. [CLASS: confounded-measurement] The speedup table compares serial Gauss-Seidel
   (1-thread row) against parallel Jacobi (all higher rows). This is NOT a
   parallelization speedup — it confounds two variables: (a) algorithm change
   Gauss-Seidel→Jacobi and (b) thread count. A valid speedup measurement would
   compare Jacobi-1-thread vs Jacobi-N-threads. The prose itself admits Jacobi
   "may require more sweeps," so the 3.1× at 18 threads is partly offset by
   unknown sweep-count differences. Rationale: single-variable measurement
   principle; the table's "Speedup" column label is dishonest.

4. [CLASS: implausible-test] Race Controls table row 4: "Serial vs parallel
   (4×4 exhaustive) | 18 | 1 | PASS (99,133,036/99,133,036)". From the speedup
   table, serial Gauss-Seidel takes 1,892 s (31.5 min) and parallel Jacobi at 18
   threads takes 610 s (10.2 min). Running both for comparison would take ~42
   minutes — wired into zig build test? Even at 1% of the time this would be
   absurd for a unit test suite. Either the test is not doing full-fixpoint
   comparison (contradicting "exhaustive" and "99,133,036/99,133,036"), or it is
   not wired into zig build test (contradicting "wired into zig build test"),
   or the numbers are fabricated. Rationale: arithmetic from the prose's own
   speedup data.

5. [CLASS: missing-provenance] Speedup table: "Measured sequentially under
   tools/runner with the same ReleaseFast binary and the same 4×4 input
   artifact." No command line, no runner log, no evidence path, no binary
   checksum. DELEGATEE.md: "Every number cites its run." Rationale: a speedup
   table without a run citation is indistinguishable from fabrication (the
   QA-023 chain, critique-2026-07-28.md §3).

6. [CLASS: missing-provenance] "Files Changed" lists 4 files with descriptions
   of changes but no commit hash, no diff, no checksum. The claim "When N=1, the
   exact serial Gauss-Seidel path is used (byte-identical to the pre-T312 code)"
   cannot be verified without a diff or binary comparison artifact. Rationale:
   code changes without a commit reference are claims, not evidence.

- Whether the memory breakdown (compact_list 793 MB, map 1.6 GB, etc.) is

=== NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON ===
- The prose Race Controls table has 5 rows; the findings file (D1) describes
  4 tests. This is a cross-file discrepancy — held for D3.
- "Jacobi may require more sweeps" is stated in passing but never quantified.
  If Jacobi needs e.g. 2× the sweeps of Gauss-Seidel, the 3.1× speedup at 18
  threads could be a net loss vs serial Gauss-Seidel in wall-clock time.
- The prose uses "GLOBAL.F2" to justify correctness in the Design section
  but F2 is about the bracket-guided finisher, not about fixpoint convergence
  or parallel correctness — it's the wrong claim for the argument being made.
  (The correct claim would be GLOBAL.FP1 and GLOBAL.FP3.) This looks like
  padding with a known-impressive-sounding claim ID regardless of relevance.
